claim: Balduzzi et al. propose Nash averaging, a game-theoretic aggregation rule proven invariant to redundant copies of tasks or agents in a benchmark evaluation suite.

quoted_support: Evaluation is often based on metrics like average performance or Elo ratings. Unfortunately, two (or two hundred) tasks or agents that look different may test/exhibit identical skills. Overrepresenting particular tasks or agents introduces biases into averages and Elo -- biases that can only be detected post hoc.
